slide.title: Implemented: exact Item selections and saved-view pins
slide.takeaway: An Item selects a subset through saved pins and a stable evidence ID; historical pins need an explicit saved view, and old pins survive definition succession.

item.label: Declared path of saved pins
item.description: Each hop must be declared by the previous saved revision: System member, holder or relationship destination. The range must lie inside the named evidence at its commit; failures have stable codes.

references.note: ResolveSelection: path, evidence and containment with reason codes.
declaresHop: only declared links at the saved revision.

criterion_links.rationale: A reference stores an inspectable subset; referencing a System selects nothing implicitly.
The saved path records the System/Component/data-entity route that coverage reports will expose.

item.label: Selected bytes authored exactly
item.description: The CLI defaults an omitted commit to the containing evidence commit, prechecks structure, then digests only the selected lines; a supplied digest must match.

references.note: authorItemLinks resolves views once and authors new selections.
defaultSelectionCommits uses the containing evidence commit.

criterion_links.rationale: Each selection stores its commit, path, exact range and selected-byte digest for display and currency checks.

item.label: Explicit saved view
item.description: A historical pin is admitted only when the Saga committed at the named commit binds it as its active current revision. The loader reads that commit through Git and refuses with a specific reason.

references.note: savedview.Load: commit, Saga identity, source and inventory at that commit.
admitDocumentationPin applies technicalpolicy.AdmitPin.

criterion_links.rationale: A review Item can pin the committed design revision through the saved view that bound it.

item.label: Old pins are retained
item.description: An unchanged pin, view or selection is retained when an Item is revised, and a newer definition revision is never substituted in a saved path.

references.note: admitItemLinks retains unchanged pins and re-resolves every selection.

criterion_links.rationale: Definition succession leaves prior Item pins and selections intact so evolution stays traceable.

item.label: Selection and view tests
item.description: Tests cover review and implementation Items, every named refusal, saved-view admission and refusal, retention across a newer revision, and transaction selections with replayed retries.

references.note: Review/implementation selections, refusals and saved views.
apply-slide selections, replay and refusal.
Structural resolution never substitutes newer revisions.

criterion_links.rationale: Review deck Items reference the same identities and select the relevant code subset.
